subject: ECONOMICS
pageTitle: Price Elasticity of Demand: Formula and Midpoint Method
description: Calculate price elasticity of demand with the midpoint method and decide whether demand is elastic or inelastic, with two worked examples.
caption: Elasticity in 7 swipes: the midpoint formula, elastic vs inelastic, and a worked example. Save this for your econ test. Free Economics study guide at precisstudy.com/economics (no sign-up).

slides.title: THE FORMULA
slides.note: Ignore the negative sign and compare to 1.

slides.title: READ THE RESULT
lines: Greater than 1: elastic (buyers react a lot)
slides.note: Necessities tend to be inelastic; luxuries tend to be elastic.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: Price rises from $10 to $12 and quantity falls from 100 to 80. Find elasticity.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: If |E| = 1.22, what happens to total revenue when the price rises?
steps: Elastic demand: quantity falls by a bigger percent than price rises

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: Elasticity is the slope of the demand curve
points: Slope depends on units; elasticity uses percentages.
Use the average (midpoint) as the base for each percent.
A steeper curve is not always more inelastic at every point.
